methods.label: Separate complete weeks from the extra days
methods.explanation:
Since \(31=4\cdot7+3\), the first 28 days contain four of every weekday. The remaining three days have the same weekday names as the first three days of the month. Those three consecutive weekdays occur five times; every other weekday occurs four times.

Monday and Wednesday must therefore either both belong to the three extra weekdays or both lie outside them.

The extra weekdays contain both only when they are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, so a Monday start works. They contain neither for a Thursday start, giving Thursday, Friday, Saturday, or a Friday start, giving Friday, Saturday, Sunday. The other starts, Tuesday, Wednesday, Saturday, and Sunday, include exactly one of Monday and Wednesday among the extra weekdays and therefore fail.

The possible starts are Monday, Thursday, and Friday: \(\boxed{3}\) choices, answer \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: Complete seven-day groups and the three-day remainder give an elementary arithmetic solution.
